\chapter{Learning Theory --- Convex Prediction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Hedge.ConvexPrediction
\section{Overview}

This module develops the \emph{convex prediction bridge} for the Hedge algorithm.
When every expert's prediction lies in a convex decision set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
and each round's loss function is convex on $S$, Jensen's inequality shows that the
loss of Hedge's weighted-average prediction is at most Hedge's abstract expected expert
loss; combining this with the abstract Hedge regret theorems yields tight, explicit
regret bounds for the real prediction-space problem.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Induced loss sequence]
\lean{inducedLoss}
\label{inducedLoss}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq}
Given a loss function $\ell : \mathbb{R} \to \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, expert predictions
$p : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$, and a sequence of outcomes
$o : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \Omega$, the \emph{induced loss sequence} is the abstract
loss table $L : \mathrm{LossSeq}\,N\,T$ defined by $L_{t,i} = \ell(p_t(i),\, o_t)$,
i.e.\ expert $i$ at round $t$ incurs the loss its own prediction receives under the
realized outcome.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hedge weighted-average prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction}
\label{hedgePrediction}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, inducedLoss}
At each round $t \in \mathrm{Fin}\,T$, Hedge's \emph{prediction in the original
decision space} is the weighted average
\[
  \widehat{x}_t \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w^{(\eta)}_{t,i}\, p_t(i),
\]
where $w^{(\eta)}_{t,i} = \texttt{hedgeDist}\,\eta\,L\,t\,i$ are the Hedge
weights computed from the induced loss table $L$ up to (but not including) round $t$,
and $p_t(i)$ is expert $i$'s prediction at round $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cumulative loss of Hedge's predictions]
\lean{hedgePredictionCumLoss}
\label{hedgePredictionCumLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgePrediction}
The \emph{actual cumulative prediction loss} of Hedge is
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T \;=\; \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right),
\]
where $\widehat{x}_t$ is the Hedge weighted-average prediction at round $t$.  This
differs from \texttt{hedgeCumLoss}: here the loss is applied to the averaged
prediction, not to a weighted average of expert losses.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Hedge prediction stays in the convex prediction set]
\lean{hedgePrediction_mem}
\label{hedgePrediction_mem}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum, hedgePrediction, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set, fix any learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, a loss
function $\ell : \bbr \to \Omega \to \bbr$, expert predictions $p_t(i)$, and a sequence
of outcomes, and suppose that every expert prediction lies in $S$, that is $p_t(i) \in
S$ for all rounds $t$ and all experts $i$. Then for every round $t$, Hedge's
weighted-average prediction $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_{i} w^{(\eta)}_{t,i}\, p_t(i)$ —
formed from the Hedge distribution of the loss table induced by $\ell$, the predictions,
and the outcomes up to round $t$ — again lies in $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bound for Hedge's weighted-average prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction_loss_le_hedgeLoss}
\label{hedgePrediction_loss_le_hedgeLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum, hedgeLoss, hedgePrediction, hedgePrediction_mem, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $N \ge 1$ experts, a horizon of $T$ rounds, a learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, and a
convex set $S \subseteq \bbr$. Let $\ell : \bbr \times \Omega \to \bbr$ be a loss
function, let $e_t(i) \in \bbr$ be expert $i$'s prediction at round $t$, and let $o_t
\in \Omega$ be the outcome at round $t$; write $L_{t,i} = \ell(e_t(i), o_t)$ for the
induced loss table and let $q_t(i)$ denote the Hedge distribution over the experts
computed from $L$ at round $t$. Suppose every prediction $e_t(i)$ lies in $S$, and that
for each round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$. Then at every
round $t$ the loss of Hedge's weighted-average prediction $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_{i}
q_t(i)\, e_t(i)$ is at most its expected loss under $q_t$:
\[
  \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} q_t(i)\, \ell\!\left(e_t(i),\, o_t\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bound for Hedge's averaged predictions]
\lean{hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss}
\label{hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePrediction_loss_le_hedgeLoss, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, a loss function $\ell : \bbr \to \Omega \to \bbr$,
expert predictions $p : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \bbr$ (with $N \ge 1$),
and a sequence of outcomes $o : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \Omega$. Suppose $S \subseteq \bbr$
is convex, every expert prediction $p_t(i)$ lies in $S$, and for each round $t$ the map
$x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$. Then the cumulative loss of Hedge's
weighted-average predictions is at most the cumulative Hedge loss computed on the
induced loss sequence:
\[
  \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \sum_{i=1}^{N} p_t(i)\,\ell\!\left(p_t(i), o_t\right),
\]
where $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_{i} p_t(i)\, p_t(i)$ is the Hedge weighted-average
prediction at round $t$ and $p_t$ is the Hedge distribution at that round.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Tight regret bound for Hedge's convex predictions]
\lean{hedgePrediction_regret_bound_tight}
\label{hedgePrediction_regret_bound_tight}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq.Valid, bestExpertLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss, hedge_regret_bound_tight, inducedLoss, regret}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set, let $\eta > 0$ be a learning rate, and consider
a prediction problem with $N \ge 1$ experts over $T$ rounds, an outcome $o_t$ at each
round $t$, and a loss function $\ell(x, o)$. Suppose that every expert prediction
$p_t(i)$ lies in $S$, that for each round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex
on $S$, and that the induced loss sequence is valid, so that each expert's per-round
loss $\ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ lies in $[0,1]$. Then the cumulative loss
$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T = \sum_{t} \ell(\widehat{x}_t, o_t)$ of Hedge's
weighted-average predictions $\widehat{x}_t$ exceeds the best expert loss in hindsight
$L^* = \min_{i} \sum_{t} \ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ by at most
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T - L^* \;\le\; \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta T}{8}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimal-rate regret bound for Hedge with convex prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction_regret_tight_optimal}
\label{hedgePrediction_regret_tight_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq.Valid, bestExpertLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss, hedge_regret_tight_optimal, inducedLoss, optimalEtaTight, regret}
\difficulty{2}
Consider prediction with expert advice using $N \ge 2$ experts over $T \ge 1$ rounds,
where predictions take values in a convex set $S \subseteq \bbr$. Let $\ell : \bbr
\times \Omega \to \bbr$ be a loss function, let $p_t(i) \in S$ be the prediction of
expert $i$ at round $t$, and let $o_t \in \Omega$ be the outcome at round $t$; assume
that for every round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$, and that all
induced losses $\ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ lie in $[0,1]$. Run the Hedge algorithm with learning
rate $\eta_{\mathrm{tight}} = \sqrt{8\ln N / T}$, predicting at each round the Hedge
weighted average $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_i p_t(i)\, w_{t}(i) \in S$, where the weights
$w_t$ form the Hedge distribution built from the induced losses through the first $t$
rounds. Then the cumulative loss of these predictions exceeds the best expert's loss in
hindsight by at most $\sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}$:
\[
\sum_{t} \ell\bigl(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\bigr) \;-\; \min_{i}\, \sum_{t}
\ell\bigl(p_t(i),\, o_t\bigr)
  \;\le\; \sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}.
\]
\end{theorem}
